title.value: On the Origin of Hallucinations in Conversational Models: Is it the Datasets or the Models?
title.justification: This title captures the main subject of the paper, which investigates the reasons behind hallucinations in conversational models.
title.quote: On the Origin of Hallucinations in Conversational Models: Is it the Datasets or the Models?

extractions.description: The paper investigates the sources of hallucinations in knowledge-grounded conversational models, focusing on whether these hallucinations stem from the training datasets or the models themselves. It conducts a human study on existing benchmarks and state-of-the-art models, revealing that significant hallucinations exist in both datasets and generated responses. The paper raises questions about data quality and model robustness in conversational systems.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on conversational AI, specifically the issue of hallucinations in models and datasets, without any direct connection to climate or ecological sustainability themes.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our findings raise important questions on the quality of existing datasets and models trained using them.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on the technical challenges in AI models and datasets rather than themes related to sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: We find that the generated responses consist of an even larger portion of hallucinations, in comparison with the training data.

secondary_categories.justification: No secondary themes are related to sustainable development, as the paper discusses AI technical issues instead.
secondary_categories.quote: This kind of optimization will likely push the models to replicate and even amplify the hallucination behaviour at test time.

primary_sub_category.justification: The content does not align with any specific sub-category related to sustainable development as it deals with dataset quality and AI hallucinations.
primary_sub_category.quote: Knowledge-grounded conversational models are known to suffer from producing factually invalid statements, a phenomenon commonly called hallucination.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: As the primary content focuses on dataset and model issues, there are no secondary sub-categories applicable to sustainable development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Hallucination: a response’s factual correctness cannot be fully verified from the knowledge-snippet (even if it is true in the real world).

applications.justification: No climate or sustainability applications are discussed, as the paper looks at AI conversational models' hallucination issues.
applications.quote: Our analysis reveals surprisingly that more than 60% of the responses are hallucinated in the three datasets.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not introduce a new sustainability category, rather it focuses on AI challenges.
new_primary_category.quote: We conduct a comprehensive human study on both existing knowledge-grounded conversational benchmarks and several state-of-the-art models.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no new sub-category relevant to sustainability as the focus is on AI technical aspects.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: To understand the linguistic nature of hallucinations, we further annotate responses based on a linguistic coding system for discourse phenomena.
